before.event: Son of Zhang Tianxi, deposed heir. [External dating, inferred: Taihe 1 corresponds to AD 366-366 by the Jin reign-year table (Taishi 1 = 265, Yongjia 1 = 307, Jianxing 1 = 313, Jianwu 1 = 317, Xianhe 1 = 326, Yonghe 1 = 345, Shengping 1 = 357, Xingning 1 = 363, Xianan 1 = 371).]

after.event: Zhang Tianxi established his son Dahuai as heir apparent.

changes.reason: s0769 立子大懷為世子 is Dahuai’s own heir appointment, narrated after the Eastern Jin 太和初 edict in s0753 (詔以天錫為大將軍…涼州刺史、西平公) and Tianxi’s return from the Li Yan campaign. That 太和 is 海西公司馬奕’s era; 太和元年 is AD 366, so the appointment stays in the 太和初 block as a year-precision interval 366–366. The old row also cited s0775 and called him a “deposed heir,” folding the later undated 廢大懷 into Taihe 1. Evidence is now only s0769; the deposition is a separate attestation.

after.event: Deposed as heir apparent and made Duke of Gaochang.

changes.reason: s0775 廢大懷為高昌公，更立嬖子大豫為世子 names Dahuai’s later deposition with no reign year, month, or day. It follows the heir appointment and a general notice that Tianxi 荒於聲色, so it is later than 太和初 but not dated. Do not assign Taihe 1, invent a death, or treat a later 初 flashback as the event year. The source attestation is explicitly undated.

The only Western-dated personal event is the 太和初 heir appointment (AD 366). s0775 attests a later deposition without a year, so the hint keeps the AD 366 attestation and records that later act as undated instead of closing his activity in 366 or inventing a death year.
